Python API Reference#

ovclash ships two peer Python packages:

  • ovclash is a thin ctypes binding over the canonical clash C ABI (ovclash.h), the engine layer’s C application binary interface.

  • ovclash_suite is the product API over the Suite C ABI: an object model, persistence and JSON/HTML export.

The wheel, the Python package file that pip installs, carries both packages, and so does the python/ directory of the SDK archive, the C/C++ and Python release package. A name that exists in both packages, such as RunSettings or backend_info, is a different object in each. The Glossary section of Concepts defines the terms this page uses. Choosing an API explains how to pick, and C API Reference documents the C contracts that both build on. The Python Quickstart runs a first query.

Both packages share one native library, which the first import loads. The Native library lookup section of ovclash Python Package gives the lookup order, the loader variables and the errors the import raises.

The wheel and the SDK archive also ship omni.physxclashdetectioncore, which exposes ovclash_suite names under their import paths in Kit (NVIDIA Omniverse Kit, the application framework of the Kit clash detection extension). This page documents the ovclash_suite originals. Kit Compatibility lists what the compatibility package exports.

The canonical binding: ovclash#

Core classes#

Async Pipelines covers AsyncPipeline. Threading and Ownership covers the lifetimes of OverlapReport and BufferView data. ovstage Integration covers borrowing a caller-owned Stage of ovstage, the runtime through which ovclash reads USD (Universal Scene Description) scenes, with ClashRuntime.attach_ovstage().

A BufferView borrows native memory that dies with its report. Copy what you keep before the report closes. This complete script opens time_sampled.usda, which the wheel ships in <site-packages>/ovclash/samples/data/ and the SDK archive in <sdk>/samples/data/, where <site-packages> is the interpreter’s package directory and <sdk> the extracted archive. Run it from that directory, or pass the stage’s full path to open_stage:

from ovclash import ClashRuntime, OverlapReportFlag

with ClashRuntime() as runtime:
    runtime.open_stage("time_sampled.usda")
    runtime.set_scope(["/Root/Xform_Primitives/Cube"], ["/Root/Xform_Primitives/Plane"])
    runtime.run_pipeline()
    flags = OverlapReportFlag.FACES0 | OverlapReportFlag.OUTLINE
    with runtime.get_overlap_report(0, flags=flags) as report:
        faces = report.faces0.numpy().copy()  # copy: the view dies with the report
        segments = report.outline.tolist()  # tolist() always copies
    print(len(faces), "faces,", len(segments), "outline segments")

4 faces, 10 outline segments
class ovclash.ClashRuntime#

Bases: object

Standalone clash runtime that owns one native context of the canonical clash C ABI.

The lifecycle follows the engine contract. open_stage() opens the stage. set_run_settings() applies the engine settings, including the requested full-scene flag, and clears the native scope. The explicit A/B scope recorded by set_scope() is applied just before the pipeline is created, so it survives that reset.

Call destroy() when done; that is the primary lifetime contract. As a context manager, a normal exit waits for an active async run, and an exit by exception cancels the run first; both then release the context. A finalizer that runs inside an ovstage owner callback defers the native cleanup and keeps the attachments alive until then.

A failed native call raises RuntimeError with the context’s last error. While an AsyncPipeline from run_async() is active, the methods that change the settings, scope or stage, run the pipeline or read results raise RuntimeError until the run is finished or cancelled. Serialize calls on one runtime; only the AsyncPipeline methods may be called from other threads. Native calls from inside an ovstage owner operation are rejected with RuntimeError.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The native context cannot be created.

attach_ovstage(
stage: Any,
committed_ordinal: int,
**metadata: Any,
) → None#

Borrow the owner’s live ovstage Stage instead of opening a file.

The metadata fields follow ovclash_ovstage_binding_t in ovclash/ovclash_ovstage.h. evaluate_time(seconds) receives NaN for the Default time and returns a newer committed ordinal. While clash operations run, the owner must exclude concurrent rendering, edits and destruction of the Stage. Without composition_root, no source filename is opened.

authored_transform_updates=True requires the C binding’s full raw-op/default-order population and same-time update provenance contract, plus an evaluator that seals a newer ordinal at identical seconds. Without that explicit capability, attached meshes stay non-static.

composition_root and composition_layers fill the binding’s ovclash_ovstage_composition_t and make the attachment engine-evaluated. Default selection reads the Stage at committed_ordinal, which must stay retained until detach. Every finite time is evaluated natively in private ovstage instances that replay the root and composition_layers, the texts of the owner’s surviving root merges in the order it added them; the Stage is never evaluated or advanced. The owner guarantees that the composition reproduces its transforms at every finite time, and keeps the root file and every file that the root or a layer references unchanged on disk while attached, because each replay reopens the root by its string. A relative root resolves against the working directory at replay time, so open the Stage from an absolute path or URL and pass that string. It requires a NaN time_seconds and no evaluate_time or authored_transform_updates.

A successful attachment replaces any previous one, drops the scope recorded by set_scope() and invalidates the pipeline. Like open_stage(), it does not restore full-scene traversal. This runtime keeps the Stage and the callback alive until detach_ovstage(), reset(), another attachment, an open_stage() call with a nonempty path, or destroy(). A failed attachment keeps the previous one.

Parameters:

  • stage – Live ovstage.Stage to borrow.

  • committed_ordinal – Positive uint64 ordinal of the Stage’s current committed evaluation.

  • **metadata – Binding fields and their defaults: time_seconds (NaN, the Default time), meters_per_unit (0.01), start_time_code and end_time_code (0.0), time_codes_per_second and frames_per_second (24.0), evaluate_time (None), authored_transform_updates (False), composition_root (None, the exact path, URL or USDA text the owner opened), composition_layers (an empty sequence of USDA texts, earliest first) and composition_root_is_usda (False).

Raises:

  • TypeError – stage is not a live ovstage.Stage, an argument has the wrong type, or a metadata keyword is unknown.

  • ValueError – committed_ordinal is not a positive uint64, authored_transform_updates is set without evaluate_time, composition layers or composition_root_is_usda are passed without a root, the root or a layer is empty, contains NUL or is not encodable as UTF-8, or a root is combined with evaluate_time, authored_transform_updates or a time_seconds other than NaN.

  • RuntimeError – The backend is OpenUSD, an async run is active, or the native attachment fails.

close() → None#

Destroy the native context owned by this runtime.

Calling it again does nothing. destroy is the primary name, matching the main object of ovclash_suite; close is an alias kept for existing callers. An active async run is finished first, and active reports are closed.

The handle is retired when the native release succeeds or when its result is lost to an interruption. An explicit native rejection keeps the handle, so the call can be retried. A failure while closing a dependent pipeline or report also keeps the context, because its native release was not attempted yet.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The native release or the close of a dependent report fails, or the call is made inside an ovstage owner operation.

create_pipeline() → list[PipelineStepData]#

Apply the recorded scope, build the pipeline and return its planned steps.

Active reports are closed.

Returns:

One PipelineStepData per step, at least seven, as get_pipeline_step_data() reports them.

Raises:

RuntimeError – An async run is active, a scope path is invalid, or the native call fails.

destroy() → None#

Destroy the native context owned by this runtime.

Calling it again does nothing. destroy is the primary name, matching the main object of ovclash_suite; close is an alias kept for existing callers. An active async run is finished first, and active reports are closed.

The handle is retired when the native release succeeds or when its result is lost to an interruption. An explicit native rejection keeps the handle, so the call can be retried. A failure while closing a dependent pipeline or report also keeps the context, because its native release was not attempted yet.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The native release or the close of a dependent report fails, or the call is made inside an ovstage owner operation.

detach_ovstage() → None#

Stop borrowing the attached Stage without destroying it.

Active reports are closed, and the results and the pipeline are invalidated. The call also forgets a stage opened with open_stage(), and it succeeds without an attachment.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The backend is OpenUSD, an async run is active, or the native detach fails.

get_duplicate(
index: int,
) → DuplicateMesh#

Return the names, hashes, triangle count and time of one duplicate mesh pair.

The names are copied, so the record outlives the results.

Parameters:

index – Index of the duplicate pair.

Returns:

The copied pair.

Raises:

  • OverflowError – index is outside the uint32 range.

  • RuntimeError – index is out of range or stale, or an async run is active.

get_duplicate_count() → int#

Return the number of duplicate mesh pairs found by the last run.

A time-sampled run finds no duplicates and reports 0.

Returns:

The number of duplicate pairs.

Raises:

RuntimeError – An async run is active, or the native query fails.

get_overlap_count() → int#

Return the number of overlap groups of the last run, one per colliding prim pair.

A cancelled run can report 0, so check AsyncPipeline.is_cancelled() before reading 0 as clash-free.

Returns:

The number of overlap groups.

Raises:

RuntimeError – An async run is active, or the native query fails.

get_overlap_details(
overlap_index: int,
record_index: int = 0,
) → OverlapDetails#

Return get_overlap_record() data plus the hashes, minimum distance and depth.

Each hash is the pair of uint64 words of a 128-bit hash, in native array order; clash_hash hashes the two prim paths. min_distance and max_local_depth are in stage units. max_local_depth is -1.0 when depth was not computed (max_local_depth_mode is DISABLED) and 0.0 for a point-vs-mesh overlap.

Parameters:

  • overlap_index – Index of the overlap group.

  • record_index – Sampled frame within the group; always 0 for a static query.

Returns:

The copied record details.

Raises:

  • OverflowError – An index is outside the uint32 range.

  • RuntimeError – An index is out of range or stale, or an async run is active.

get_overlap_record(
overlap_index: int,
record_index: int = 0,
) → OverlapRecord#

Return the names, counts, type and time of one overlap record.

The names are copied, so the record outlives the results. time is in seconds.

Parameters:

  • overlap_index – Index of the overlap group.

  • record_index – Sampled frame within the group; always 0 for a static query.

Returns:

The copied record.

Raises:

  • OverflowError – An index is outside the uint32 range.

  • RuntimeError – An index is out of range or stale, or an async run is active.

get_overlap_report(
overlap_index: int,
*,
record_index: int = 0,
flags: ~ovclash.python.api.types.OverlapReportFlag = <OverlapReportFlag.OUTLINE|FACES0|FACES1|POINTS0: 30>,
) → OverlapReport#

Build the detailed geometry report of one overlap frame.

The default flags request every content buffer that this entry point can fill: FACES0, FACES1, OUTLINE and POINTS0. Explicit flags narrow the work. OverlapReportFlag.DEFAULT (0) and FACES select nothing here, so flags without a content bit raise ValueError; an empty report would read as “this clash touches no geometry”. Close the returned report, or use it as a context manager.

Parameters:

  • overlap_index – Index of the overlap group.

  • record_index – Sampled frame within the group; always 0 for a static query.

  • flags – OverlapReportFlag bits that select the buffers to fill.

Returns:

The open report.

Raises:

  • ValueError – flags has no content bit.

  • OverflowError – An index is outside the uint32 range.

  • RuntimeError – An async run is active, or the native report fails.

get_ovstage_matrix_decomposition() → str#

Return the matrix decomposition selected for this ovstage context.

Returns:

"openusd" or "ovclash".

Raises:

RuntimeError – The backend is OpenUSD, or the native call fails or reports an unknown mode.

get_pipeline_step_data(
step_index: int,
) → PipelineStepData#

Return the planned description of one pipeline step, not live progress.

progress is step_index / nb_steps, step_progress is 0.0 and finished is True only for the last step.

Parameters:

step_index – Index of the step in the created pipeline.

Returns:

The planned step.

Raises:

  • OverflowError – step_index is outside the uint32 range.

  • RuntimeError – step_index is outside the created pipeline, or an async run is active.

get_query_stats() → QueryStats#

Return the mesh, shared-mesh, cooked-mesh and point-cloud counts of the last run.

On ovstage, nb_cooked_meshes below nb_meshes - nb_shared_meshes means that meshes that could not be cooked were dropped from the results; see ovclash_stats_t.

Returns:

The counts.

Raises:

RuntimeError – An async run is active, or the native query fails.

get_run_settings() → RunSettings#

Read back the settings currently applied to the native context.

This is the inverse of set_run_settings(). A new runtime reports the engine defaults, which differ from RunSettings().

The native context has no set_times flag, so set_times reads back True only when a native time is non-zero. After set_run_settings() with set_times=False, and on a new runtime, all three times are 0.0. The readback then has set_times=False and time_codes_per_second=0.0. Enabling a dynamic range from that readback keeps the 0.0 rate, so the run takes one sample at start_time; pass time_codes_per_second too.

Returns:

The applied settings, limited to the fields that RunSettings models.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The native call fails.

get_stage_timeline_data() → StageTimelineData#

Read the root-layer timeline metadata of the open stage.

A Stage attached with attach_ovstage() reports the timeline fields of its attachment instead.

Returns:

The timeline metadata, as USD resolves it for an opened file.

Raises:

RuntimeError – No stage is open or attached, an async run is active, or the native query fails.

last_error() → str#

Return a copy of the context’s last error message.

Successful calls do not always clear the message, so read it only after a call failed.

Returns:

The message, or an empty string when there is none or the context is destroyed.

open_stage(stage_path: str) → None#

Open a USD stage file.

A nonempty path detaches a borrowed ovstage Stage first, so the Stage stays detached even when the open fails. An empty path or a path that cannot be encoded keeps the borrowed Stage. A missing file or a USD or ovstage open error also drops the stage that was open before.

A successful open drops the scope recorded by set_scope(), because both backends clear the native scope there. A failed open keeps the recorded scope, as the Suite runtime does.

Opening does not restore full-scene traversal. Once create_pipeline has applied a non-empty scope, enable_full_scene stays cleared until set_run_settings enables it again. Until then, the next run on the new stage selects nothing and reports zero overlaps with a success status. Record a new scope with set_scope(), or call runtime.set_run_settings(runtime.get_run_settings(), enable_full_scene=True) to traverse the whole stage again. Passing get_run_settings() as the base keeps the other RunSettings fields; a call without a base starts from the RunSettings() defaults.

Parameters:

stage_path – Local path of the stage file; asset URIs are rejected.

Raises:

  • RuntimeError – The open fails, or an async run is active.

  • UnicodeEncodeError – stage_path cannot be encoded as UTF-8.

reset() → None#

Drop all results; keep the settings, the opened stage file and the recorded scope.

Like ovclash_reset_context, which keeps the native scope, this keeps the scope recorded by set_scope(), so create_pipeline applies it again after a later set_run_settings. A borrowed ovstage Stage is detached, and active reports are closed.

Raises:

RuntimeError – An async run is active, or the native reset fails.

run_async() → AsyncPipeline#

Start the pipeline on a background worker.

Creates the pipeline first when none is cached, and closes active reports. The Python owner of the run exists before the native launch. When the launch or its result handling raises, the worker is drained, if possible, before the exception propagates; that cleanup can block until the worker finishes. Only one async run exists per runtime.

Returns:

The run handle. Finish, cancel or close it before most other methods of this runtime work again.

Raises:

RuntimeError – An async run is already active, or the pipeline cannot be created or started.

run_pipeline() → list[PipelineStepData]#

Create the pipeline and run every step on the calling thread.

Returns:

The planned steps, as create_pipeline() returns them.

Raises:

RuntimeError – Creating the pipeline or running a step fails.

run_pipeline_step(step_index: int) → None#

Run one pipeline step synchronously.

Active reports are closed first. Run the steps in ascending order from 0; out-of-order execution is not diagnosed.

Parameters:

step_index – Index of the step to run.

Raises:

  • OverflowError – step_index is outside the uint32 range.

  • RuntimeError – The native step is rejected or, on ovstage, fails, or an async run is active.

set_ovstage_dynamic_matrix_cache(enabled: bool) → None#

Enable or disable the sampled transform cache of ovstage.

Authored-transform classification defers matrix reads to bounded playback windows, at most 32 copied frames across the current and prefetched windows. Eligible parallel playback can prepare the next window in the background; both windows share the cache byte budget. Disabling the cache also disables prefetch and reads one frame at a time. Unresolved authored values keep sampled pose validation but are conservatively treated as non-static, because sampled pose comparisons cannot prove them static. This control does not change the reported sample times or poses.

The cache is on for a new context. Calling this closes active reports and invalidates the pipeline.

Parameters:

enabled – True to enable the cache.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The backend is OpenUSD and does not export the setter, an async run is active, or the native call fails.

set_ovstage_matrix_decomposition(
implementation: str,
) → None#

Select the matrix decomposition, "openusd" (the default) or "ovclash".

This ovstage-only setting belongs to the context and survives reset and stage replacement. A change clears results, closes active reports and invalidates the pipeline; the next run_pipeline() or run_async() creates it again. Selecting the current mode again keeps the reports and the pipeline. Immediate mesh queries also use this setting. The "ovclash" math can change zero-tolerance clash membership. A call fails while an async handle is active, even after its worker stops and when the current mode is selected again.

Both modes reject non-finite matrix values, values or linear row magnitudes outside the float range, and invalid resulting poses or scales. That includes finite rotation quaternions that are not unit length: the affected query fails instead of normalizing the rotation.

Parameters:

implementation – "openusd" or "ovclash".

Raises:

  • ValueError – implementation names another mode.

  • RuntimeError – The backend is OpenUSD, an async run is active, or the native call fails.

set_run_settings(
settings: RunSettings | None = None,
**kwargs: Any,
) → RunSettings#

Apply settings with the fields given in kwargs replaced.

Canonical settings that RunSettings does not model are reset to the ovclash_reset_settings() defaults instead of being kept from the context. The time fields are applied only when set_times is True; otherwise all three native times are 0.0, which selects a static query.

Applying settings clears the native scope; create_pipeline() applies the scope recorded by set_scope() again. It also closes active reports and invalidates the pipeline, but keeps completed results. A rejected call leaves the previous settings in place.

Parameters:

  • settings – Base settings. None starts from RunSettings().

  • **kwargs – RunSettings fields that replace the values of settings.

Returns:

The effective settings.

Raises:

  • TypeError – A keyword is not a RunSettings field.

  • ValueError – A value is out of range or not finite.

  • RuntimeError – An async run is active, or the native call fails.

set_scope(
prim_paths1: Iterable[str],
prim_paths2: Iterable[str] = (),
) → None#

Record the explicit A/B scope.

The scope is applied to the engine just before create_pipeline builds the pipeline, because set_run_settings applies the requested full-scene flag and clears any native scope applied earlier. Settings and this recorded scope may therefore be set in either order. A successful open_stage or attach_ovstage drops the recorded scope, because both backends clear their native scope there; reset keeps it, like ovclash_reset_context. Invalid paths raise RuntimeError from create_pipeline, not here.

Two empty sequences clear the scope, as in ovclash_set_scope_paths. Clearing the scope does not return to full-scene traversal, because applying a non-empty scope clears OVCLASH_SETTINGS_FLAG_FULL_SCENE. To traverse the whole stage again, call both set_scope([], []) and set_run_settings(enable_full_scene=True), in either order, before the pipeline is built again. Pass get_run_settings() as the set_run_settings base to keep the other RunSettings fields.

Parameters:

  • prim_paths1 – Absolute USD prim paths of search set A. An entry also covers the descendants of its prim.

  • prim_paths2 – Absolute USD prim paths of search set B, with the same rule.

Raises:

RuntimeError – An async run is active.

class ovclash.AsyncPipeline(
runtime: ClashRuntime,
handle: c_void_p,
)#

Bases: object

Handle to a clash pipeline running in the background.

ClashRuntime.run_async() creates it. The methods may be called from several threads. A call that overlaps a finish() running on another thread never uses the async cookie that the finish is freeing. is_running(), is_cancelled() and step_data() then answer from the state latched here, and finish(), cancel() and close() wait for that finish to return. So cancel() cannot interrupt a finish() that is already waiting on another thread. To cancel from a UI, poll and cancel on one thread, and call finish() on that thread once the loop ends.

As a context manager, it waits for the run on normal exit, and cancels and drains it when the block raises. Neither exit raises for a failed or cancelled run; call finish() to have a failed run raise.

Parameters:

  • runtime – Runtime that started the run.

  • handle – Async cookie that ovclash_run_pipeline_async fills.

cancel() → None#

Request cancellation of a running pipeline and finish it.

The canonical C ABI frees the async cookie only in finish, so this requests the stop and then finishes the run. It blocks until the worker exits, which releases the runtime guard. Finishing also clears the native cancel flag, so the request is latched here and is_cancelled() keeps reporting it. The cancelled outcome does not raise. Once the pipeline is finished, this does nothing.

A finish() already waiting on another thread cannot be interrupted, because the cookie that a cancel request needs may be freed at any moment. This then requests nothing and only waits for that finish, which keeps its own outcome.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The native cancel request fails, or the call is made inside an ovstage owner operation.

close() → None#

Finish the run if it was never finished, without raising for its outcome.

Blocks until the worker exits, or until a finish running on another thread returns. An Exception raised while finishing is suppressed, and the handle is retired either way.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The call is made inside an ovstage owner operation.

finish() → None#

Block until the run completes, then release the async handle.

The results are readable through the runtime afterwards. ovclash_finish_pipeline deletes the async cookie, so this object never uses it again. A later call waits for a finish in progress on another thread, and otherwise returns at once without raising. cancel() finishes the run itself, so a later finish() does not raise.

Once the native finish is attempted, the handle is retired even when an interruption or the Python result processing raises. Such an exception does not mean that the run succeeded, and later calls, which do nothing, do not change that outcome. Destroy the runtime when the outcome of an interrupted cleanup is uncertain.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The run failed, or cancellation was requested before the finish, for example by the broadphase limit. The message holds the context’s last error. Also raised when the call is made inside an ovstage owner operation.

is_cancelled() → bool#

Return whether cancellation was requested for this run.

Once True, this stays True, also after the pipeline is finished. A caller can therefore make the cross-check that ovclash.h prescribes before trusting a zero overlap count.

The native flag cannot answer alone: ovclash_finish_pipeline frees the async cookie and clears the flag, and cancel() must finish the run to release the runtime guard. So the native flag is read only while the cookie is live. Once the cookie is gone, or while another thread’s finish() frees it, this answers from the latch.

Returns:

True when cancellation was requested.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The native query fails.

is_running() → bool#

Return whether the run is still going.

A cancelled, finished or closed pipeline is not running, so this returns False instead of calling through the released cookie, and poll() keeps working after teardown. The native poll also reports False as soon as cancellation is requested, before the worker stops; only finish() waits for the worker.

While another thread’s finish() waits for the run, the results are not readable yet. This then returns True unless cancellation was requested, as the native poll would.

Returns:

True while the run is going.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The native query fails.

poll() → tuple[bool, PipelineStepData]#

Return (is_running(), step_data()).

step_data().finished marks the last step index, not a completed run. Drive a poll loop by the running flag, then call finish().

Returns:

The running flag and the current or last observed step.

Raises:

RuntimeError – Either query fails.

step_data() → PipelineStepData#

Return the current step of the run, or the last one observed once the run is over.

After cancel(), finish() or close(), the async cookie that every native getter needs is gone, so this answers from a latch. A caller draining a poll loop then gets the final step instead of an error on its last iteration.

A successful read fills the latch, and a successful finish settles it. A completed run reports finished=True at full progress, so the last poll() of a drained loop does not report “not running, not finished”. Settling rewrites the cached record locally. Teardown never reads through the handle to refresh it: teardown also runs on pipelines whose handle is already unusable, and such a read crashes the process instead of raising a clean error.

A cancelled run is not settled. It did not finish, so the latch keeps the last step actually observed; check is_cancelled(). While another thread’s finish() waits for the run, this also answers from the latch.

Returns:

The current or last observed step.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The native query fails, or the cookie is gone or being finished and no step was ever read.

class ovclash.OverlapReport(
runtime: ClashRuntime,
overlap_index: int,
record_index: int,
flags: int,
)#

Bases: object

Detailed geometry of one overlap record: colliding faces, outline segments and points.

ClashRuntime.get_overlap_report() creates reports through ovclash_create_overlap_report_ex, which also returns the world transforms of both prims for that record. A report has these attributes:

  • faces0 and faces1: BufferView of uint32 USD face indices of mesh 0 and mesh 1 (flags FACES0 and FACES1).

  • outline: BufferView of float32 with shape (n, 6). Each row is one segment x0, y0, z0, x1, y1, z1 (flag OUTLINE).

  • points0: BufferView of uint32 USD point indices of point cloud 0 (flag POINTS0).

  • point_size0: point width (diameter) in stage units, without the prim’s transform scaling. It is 0.0 when the cloud authors per-point widths, except that ovstage reports a uniform per-point array as its single value.

  • matrix0 and matrix1: tuples of 16 floats, the row-major 4x4 world transforms of the two prims.

A buffer whose flag was not requested is empty. The buffer views borrow library-owned memory. The runtime closes its active reports before any call that changes its stage, settings, scope or pipeline, and on reset and destroy. The views of a closed report raise RuntimeError, but arrays already exported from them dangle. Consume or copy the buffers before those calls.

Parameters:

  • runtime – Runtime whose results the report reads.

  • overlap_index – Index of the overlap group.

  • record_index – Sampled frame within the group.

  • flags – OverlapReportFlag bits that select the buffers to fill.

Raises:

  • OverflowError – An index is outside the uint32 range.

  • RuntimeError – The native report fails.

close() → None#

Release the native report and invalidate its buffer views.

Calling it again does nothing. The views are invalidated even when the release raises. A failed release is not retried, because the native call may already have freed the buffers; when the failure happened before the call reached native code, OpenUSD report memory can stay allocated. Copy exported arrays before closing.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The native release fails, or the call is made inside an ovstage owner operation.

class ovclash.BufferView(
owner: Any,
pointer: Any,
count: int,
ctype: Any,
warp_dtype_name: str,
*,
components: int = 1,
)#

Bases: object

Buffer view with an explicit lifetime, backed by an ovclash overlap report.

The view borrows library-owned memory that is valid only until the owning OverlapReport is released. Consume or copy the data before the report is closed. After the report closes, every accessor raises RuntimeError. Arrays already exported through numpy(), warp() or DLPack are not tracked and dangle.

Parameters:

  • owner – Report that owns the memory. The view stops working once the report is closed.

  • pointer – ctypes pointer to the first element, or None or a null pointer for an empty buffer.

  • count – Number of elements.

  • ctype – ctypes type of one component, such as ctypes.c_uint32.

  • warp_dtype_name – Name of the Warp dtype of one component, "uint32" or "float32".

  • components – Number of components per element, for example 6 for outline segments.

__bool__() → bool#

Return True when the buffer has a non-null address and at least one element.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The owning report is closed.

__dlpack__(
*,
stream=None,
max_version=None,
dl_device=None,
copy=None,
)#

Export the buffer as a DLPack capsule without copying.

This implements the array-interchange protocol, so torch.from_dlpack(view), np.from_dlpack(view) and similar calls consume report buffers directly. The capsule aliases library-owned memory that stays valid only while the owning report is open, like numpy() and warp(). Consume it, or copy out of it, before the report is released.

max_version, dl_device and copy are passed on to NumPy when they are not None. NumPy older than 2.1 does not accept them, and they are then dropped.

Parameters:

  • stream – Accepted and ignored. The data is host memory, so there is no stream to synchronize with.

  • max_version – Highest DLPack version that the consumer supports.

  • dl_device – Device that the consumer requests.

  • copy – Copy request of the consumer.

Returns:

The DLPack capsule.

Raises:

RuntimeError – NumPy is not installed, or the owning report is closed.

__dlpack_device__() → tuple[int, int]#

Return the DLPack device of the buffer, which is always host memory.

Returns:

(1, 0), where 1 is kDLCPU in the DLPack device enum.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The owning report is closed.

__len__() → int#

Return the number of elements.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The owning report is closed.

property address: int#

Address of the first element, or 0 when the pointer is null.

property components: int#

Number of components per element.

property count: int#

Number of elements; a multi-component element counts once.

numpy() → Any#

Return a zero-copy NumPy array, valid only while the owning report is open.

Copy the array before closing the report or advancing its runtime’s pipeline, which closes active reports before it changes native results.

Returns:

The array, with the shape of the buffer. An empty buffer gives a new empty array.

Raises:

RuntimeError – NumPy is not installed, or the owning report is closed.

property shape: tuple[int, ...]#

Shape of the data, (count,) or (count, components).

tolist() → list[Any]#

Copy the buffer into a list.

Returns:

The values, or one list of components per element for a multi-component buffer. An empty buffer gives an empty list.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The owning report is closed.

warp() → Any#

Return a zero-copy CPU warp.array, valid only while the owning report is open.

The array references the report, but closing the report, directly or through its runtime, still invalidates the array.

Returns:

The Warp array, with the shape of the buffer.

Raises:

RuntimeError – Warp is not installed, or the owning report is closed.

Types and enums#

ovclash exports every type of this section except StageTimelineData. Import that one from ovclash.types, an alias of ovclash.python.api.types, which is the module documented here.

These dataclasses mirror a C struct of the C API Reference, with snake_case field names:

Python type

C struct

BackendInfo

ovclash_backend_info_t

PipelineStepData

ovclash_step_data_t

OverlapRecord, OverlapDetails

ovclash_overlap_data_t

DuplicateMesh

ovclash_duplicate_mesh_data_t

QueryStats

ovclash_stats_t

The class docstrings that this section renders describe every field, including the Python conversions such as the hash tuples and the bool flags. BackendInfo.native_library_path has no C counterpart.

Public data types of the canonical clash binding (ovclash).

The types mirror the curated surface of the ovclash Suite, but ClashRuntime fills them from the canonical clash C ABI (ovclash.h) instead of the Suite ABI. ovclash.types is an alias of this module.

)#

Bases: object

Curated clash run settings, mapped onto ovclash_settings_t.

Only the settings that standalone clash queries commonly tune are exposed here. The other canonical settings, such as coplanar handling, tight bounds, permanent-overlap purging and the epsilons, keep the values that ovclash_reset_settings produces. Values are checked when ClashRuntime.set_run_settings applies them, not on construction. Every float field must be finite.

The threading controls are single_threaded, new_task_manager and nb_tasks. None of them changes which pairs overlap or the per-pair data. A task count is not an exact OS-thread count.

Parameters:

  • enable_log – Print the backend’s progress and diagnostic lines to stdout.

  • enable_full_scene – Traverse the whole stage when no scope is applied.

  • enable_point_clouds – Also run point-cloud-vs-mesh queries.

  • ignore_invisible_prims – Exclude invisible prims from the selection.

  • use_usdrt – Stored and read back only; it has no effect in standalone ovclash.

  • single_threaded – Force serial execution on both backends. On ovstage the result order stays the same; on OpenUSD it may differ.

  • only_find_duplicates – Run duplicate-mesh detection only and skip overlap detection. A time-sampled run finds no duplicates.

  • set_times – Apply start_time, end_time and time_codes_per_second. When False, the query is static.

  • start_time – Start of the sampled range, in seconds, not USD time codes.

  • end_time – End of the sampled range, in seconds. It must not be below start_time when set_times is True; equal values select a single-sample query.

  • time_codes_per_second – Query samples per second, not the stage’s time-code rate. It must be finite and non-negative; 0 collapses the range to one sample.

  • tolerance – Clearance distance in stage units; mesh pairs closer than this count as clashing. 0.0 reports touching or interpenetrating geometry only.

  • max_local_depth_mode – Max-local-depth computation mode. DISABLED leaves the mesh-vs-mesh max_local_depth at -1.0, which means not computed.

  • new_task_manager – Use the new task manager, which ignores nb_tasks. On ovstage it selects Carbonite workers, and False selects std::thread workers. On OpenUSD, detection uses Carbonite under both managers, and False runs report extraction on std::thread workers.

  • nb_tasks – Task count of the legacy task manager. On OpenUSD it sets the detection task split and bounds the std::thread report-extraction workers; on ovstage it bounds the std::thread workers. Hardware concurrency and the available work bound them too. It must be in 1..255 when single_threaded and new_task_manager are both False.

The Threading section of Performance describes what the single_threaded, new_task_manager and nb_tasks fields of RunSettings control on each backend, the scene-reading implementation that the native library was built with.

The product API: ovclash_suite#

import ovclash_suite is an alias of ovclash.python.suite, the module documented in this section. Every name shown with an ovclash.python.suite. prefix is reachable as ovclash_suite.<name>. The types under Suite types and enums are also exported at the top level, for example ovclash_suite.SettingId.

Runtime#

  • Async Pipelines covers AsyncPipeline.

  • Persistence covers fetch-and-save, which writes the clash records of a completed run into a store.

  • The Suite fetch and cursor lifetime section of Threading and Ownership covers the AsyncFetchAndSave that ClashDetection.run_async_fetch_and_save() returns.

  • ovstage Integration covers ClashDetection.attach_ovstage() and run_ovstage_owner_operation().

class ovclash.python.suite.ClashDetection(backend: str = 'ovclash')#

Legacy-compatible clash detection runtime backed by the Suite C ABI.

Serialize calls that share this runtime. A started fetch iterator reserves the runtime until it is exhausted or explicitly closed, even while it is suspended after its final progress yield. While the runtime is reserved, it rejects destroy and reset, stage, settings and scope changes, pipeline execution and depth computation. A synchronous fetch keeps result reads available; an async fetch also rejects reads until its operation closes. Finish asynchronous detection before starting a fetch. Separate runtime reports still need their documented cleanup.

Explicit destroy() is the primary lifetime contract. A finalizer that runs inside an owner callback defers the native cleanup and keeps the attachments.

Parameters:

backend – Compatibility name, one of “ovclash”, “suite” or “legacy”. It does not select a backend; the loaded native library determines that.

Raises:

  • ValueError – backend is not an accepted name.

  • RuntimeError – The native runtime cannot be created.

Default value of each run setting, keyed by SettingId, read from the native defaults.

attach_ovstage(
stage: Any,
committed_ordinal: int,
**metadata: Any,
) → None#

Borrow a live ovstage.Stage under its owner’s exclusive query lease.

The metadata names match the C binding descriptor. evaluate_time(seconds) receives NaN for the Default time and returns a newly committed ordinal. The Stage, the callback and the composition buffers are kept until a successful detachment, a reset, destruction, a successful file open or another attachment. A successful attachment replaces any open file or previous binding, and clears the scope, results and pipeline. The owner must keep the Stage live and exclude rendering and edits while attached operations run. Without composition_root, no source file name is consulted.

authored_transform_updates=True opts into static-pair pruning. Use it only for owners that meet the full contract of the C binding for raw-op and default-order population and for same-time update provenance. It requires evaluate_time, and that callback must publish a newer ordinal even for identical seconds. The default leaves attached meshes conservatively non-static.

composition_root makes the attachment engine-evaluated instead. Default selection still reads the Stage at committed_ordinal, which the owner keeps retained until detach. Every finite time is evaluated natively in private ovstage instances that replay the root and composition_layers, the texts of the owner’s surviving root merges in the order it added them. The Stage is never evaluated or advanced, so the owner’s time stays where it is. The owner guarantees that the composition reproduces its transforms at every finite time, and keeps the root file and every file that the root or a layer references unchanged on disk while attached, because each replay reopens the root by its string. A relative root resolves against the working directory at replay time, so open the Stage from an absolute path or URL and pass that string. time_seconds must stay NaN, and evaluate_time and authored_transform_updates must stay unset; classification then prunes static pairs from the private population.

Parameters:

  • stage – Live ovstage.Stage to borrow.

  • committed_ordinal – Positive uint64 read ordinal of the current evaluation of the Stage.

  • **metadata – Keyword-only binding fields and their defaults: time_seconds (NaN, the Default time), meters_per_unit (0.01), start_time_code and end_time_code (0.0), time_codes_per_second and frames_per_second (24.0), evaluate_time (None), authored_transform_updates (False), composition_root (None, the exact path, URL or USDA text the owner opened), composition_layers (an empty sequence of USDA texts, earliest first) and composition_root_is_usda (False).

Raises:

  • TypeError – stage is not a live ovstage.Stage, committed_ordinal is not an integer, an unknown metadata keyword is passed, evaluate_time is not callable, authored_transform_updates or composition_root_is_usda is not a bool, composition_root is not a str or path-like object (a str for USDA), or composition_layers is a str, a set, or holds anything but str.

  • RuntimeError – An async operation is alive, the ovstage backend extension is missing, or the native attachment fails.

close() → None#

Destroy the native runtime handle that this object owns.

An unfinished async pipeline is closed first. Closing finishes it rather than cancelling it, and blocks until it completes; cancel it first to stop early. A failed cleanup of a dependent async operation leaves the runtime owned. A failed finalizer cleanup can still be recovered after the native handle of this runtime was consumed, when its async operation keeps a data store. Close fetch iterators first. close() is an alias.

fetch_and_save_overlaps(
stage: Any,
clash_data: Any,
clash_query: ClashQuery,
timing_callback: Any = None,
*,
progress_callback: Any = None,
async_mode: bool = False,
) → Iterator[float]#

Persist the runtime results and yield bounded progress, synchronously or by polling.

This is a lazy generator. The argument checks, the native launch or synchronous begin, and the settings snapshot happen on the first iteration, not when the generator is created. In async mode, initialization then runs on the background worker.

With update_clash_states_after_detection enabled (the default), re-detected normal and duplicate overlaps become ACTIVE, except an APPROVED clash whose detected contents are exactly unchanged, and absent clashes become RESOLVED. Equality compares the type, tolerance, depth epsilon, object paths and mesh checksums, the aggregate results and the complete ordered frame history, including times, matrices, metrics and geometry payload. Stored overlap and frame row identifiers, review fields, timestamps and user penetration-depth annotations do not take part. The query and the ordered pair hash establish result identity; a matching overlap hash alone does not prove unchanged contents.

The numeric comparison uses no epsilon, treats signed zeros as equal and NaNs as unequal, and does not depend on the caller’s denormal controls. It compares at ABI precision: float32 for outlines and point sizes, float64 for header values, frame scalar metrics, times and matrices. The SQLite, directory and Python custom serializers provide the stored-result reader for this comparison. Disable the flag to preserve stored states. New overlaps start NEW and are not promoted during their first fetch. Absent clashes are marked not present in either mode.

Native operations reserve their runtime and native data store until they are destroyed, even after completion or failure. While that reservation exists, resetting or destroying the runtime and modifying, reopening, saving-as or closing the store is rejected. Close an abandoned iterator before closing the data store or destroying the runtime.

Each native step attempts at most 1024 runtime frame reports across approval comparison and capture, and stops once it reaches 8 MiB of runtime report payload; one indivisible report may exceed that threshold. Long overlaps span several steps, and no borrowed report or preparation worker stays alive between steps. Async mode drives the steps on one persistence worker. Its polling yields may occur during initialization, a native step or cleanup, and busy runtime or data reads are rejected. Modification notifications use a path cached before the launch. Duplicate persistence follows SETTING_DUP_MESHES of this query, independently of the runtime’s only_find_duplicates setting. Fetch preparation uses the threading settings that the runtime has at native initialization.

Fetch-and-save is not all-or-nothing for every failure:

  • A serializer callback failure while the fetch advances, including a saved-result reader failure, requests a rollback of the whole pending transaction. That includes earlier batches and other uncommitted changes on the same destination.

  • An initialization failure leaves pre-existing writes pending.

  • An extraction, frame-preparation or scheduling failure restores only an incomplete streamed overlap and keeps earlier completed pending writes. A failed overlap cleanup falls back to a full rollback.

  • A cancellation or an iterator close also leaves completed writes pending when the cleanup succeeds. An explicit iterator close raises on a failed cleanup; an earlier processing exception stays primary during unwinding.

The SQLite and directory stores attempt to commit retained pending writes when they close or are destroyed, so an exception or an abandoned iterator can still leave partial results on disk.

A successful native completion reconciles absent overlaps, calls the idempotent BEGIN and commits before it yields 1.0, even for an empty result; pending writes are published too. Reconciliation can span several steps. Stopping synchronous iteration, or a cancellation that the async worker observes before the commit, leaves the absent-state updates applied so far pending and performs no further reconciliation. Stopping async polling alone leaves the worker running; close requests cancellation and drains it. A cancellation can race a successful commit and does not undo committed results.

After the final 1.0 yield, exhaust or explicitly close the iterator to release its runtime and store leases. A modification-notification callback can raise after that commit, and timing_callback runs after the iteration completes; either exception leaves the committed results intact. A failed native operation cannot resume; a retry must start a new iterator. Custom serializers must implement the same transaction and savepoint contract. The threading mode does not change these rules.

Parameters:

  • stage – Kept for caller compatibility; the results come from the runtime.

  • clash_data – Open Suite serializer or its ClashData facade. Custom serializers implement the AbstractClashDataSerializer fetch hooks; native code owns scheduling and reconciliation for every serializer.

  • clash_query – Query that owns the fetched overlaps.

  • timing_callback – Optional callable that receives (level, name, seconds, detail) timing rows.

  • progress_callback – Optional callable that receives exact (written, total) result-group counts after initialization and after each modification notification. Synchronous mode reports after each native step; async mode reports polling snapshots and always reports the final counts. The first call is (0, total). The counts include the query’s selected duplicates and exclude old rows and incomplete streamed overlaps. Written results may still be pending; written == total does not imply a commit. The final reconciliation and commit precede the 1.0 progress yield. The callable runs on the iterating thread while the runtime and destination stay reserved. Its exception closes the operation and propagates; committed results are kept, and earlier pending writes follow the cancellation rules above. The float progress yields are unchanged.

  • async_mode – Run the persistence on a native worker and yield polling progress. Custom serializers then opt into callbacks on the worker thread. Progress, modification and timing callbacks stay on the iterating thread.

Yields:

Progress between 0.0 and 1.0; the last yield of a successful fetch is 1.0.

Raises:

  • TypeError – progress_callback is neither callable nor None.

  • ValueError – clash_data is None. This method persists results and does not run detection; when persistence is not needed, run the pipeline and read its results directly.

  • NotImplementedError – A custom serializer does not override fetch_transaction().

  • RuntimeError – Another async operation is alive, clash_data is not an open Suite serializer, or a native fetch call fails.

static is_depth_computation_supported(
overlap_type: OverlapType,
) → bool#

Return whether depth computations are available for an overlap type.

compute_max_local_depth() and compute_penetration_depth() resolve both paths as meshes, so a point-cloud-vs-mesh overlap cannot be computed. Call this check before either of them; neither tests the overlap type itself.

Only POINT_CLOUD_MESH is rejected. UNDEFINED (0x7fffffff) returns True: an overlap whose type was never classified is not known to be a point cloud, and the compute methods still raise when a path does not resolve to a mesh.

Parameters:

overlap_type – An ovclash_suite.OverlapType, for example ClashInfo.overlap_type. Do not pass ovclash.OverlapType from the canonical binding. The two enums are unrelated and their point-cloud members differ in value (ovclash_suite POINT_CLOUD_MESH is 3, ovclash POINT_VS_MESH is 1). A canonical value is compared by number, so a point-cloud overlap would be reported as supported.

Returns:

True when the depth computations can run for such an overlap.

stage: Any = None,
*,
time_codes_per_second: float | None = None,

Apply legacy setting values to the native runtime.

Parameters:

  • settings – Setting values keyed by SettingId member, its integer value or its name, such as "SETTING_TOLERANCE". Other keys are ignored without an error. A missing setting takes its DEFAULT_SETTINGS value.

  • stage – Optional legacy Python stage object, used only to open the same file-backed stage and to derive the time settings. When it names the open file, resolved from the current directory, the file is not reopened and the scope from set_scope_paths() is kept. Any spelling of the open file counts: its open path, a pathlib.Path or a layer’s absolute realPath. After a failed open dropped the stage, any spelling opens the file again, the repeated path included. Any other file is opened as by open_stage(), which drops the scope. C callers set the time fields of ovclash_suite_run_settings_t instead.

  • time_codes_per_second – Optional sampling rate of a dynamic run, in samples per second. The default is the open stage’s own timeCodesPerSecond. The seconds that the query times resolve to do not change. C callers set ovclash_suite_run_settings_t.time_codes_per_second directly.

Returns:

True when the native runtime accepts the settings.

Raises:

  • RuntimeError – An async operation is alive, stage cannot be opened, an attached ovstage Stage reports no timeline, a dynamic query on a binary crate stage has neither a readable timeline nor an explicit range, or the C ABI rejects the settings.

  • ValueError – time_codes_per_second is given and is not a positive number, a resolved value is out of range or not finite, stage names no file while none is open, or stage is not the attached ovstage Stage.

A non-empty path that encodes successfully first detaches a borrowed Stage, and a later file-open failure leaves this runtime detached. An empty path, or a path that fails to encode, keeps the borrowed binding. A successful open drops the scope set by set_scope_paths(), even when it reopens the file that is already open; a failed open keeps it.

Parameters:

stage_path – Filesystem path of the USD stage.

Returns:

True when the stage opened; False when the native open fails (see last_error()).

Raises:

RuntimeError – An async operation is alive, or detaching a borrowed Stage fails.

)#

Bases: object

Handle of a Suite clash pipeline that runs asynchronously.

ClashDetection.run_async_pipeline() creates it. While the handle is alive, the runtime rejects other work; finish, cancel or close the handle first.

Parameters:

  • runtime – ClashDetection that started the pipeline.

  • handle – Native async handle from ovclash_suite_run_pipeline_async. This object owns it and releases it with ovclash_suite_async_destroy.

cancel() → None#

Request cancellation, drain the execution and release the native async cookie.

A call after the handle is released does nothing.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The native cancel or the handle release fails.

close() → None#

Release the native asynchronous pipeline handle.

An unfinished run is finished first, which blocks until it completes; call cancel() to stop it early. An explicit native destroy failure keeps the handle for retry. When a Python exception hides the native outcome, the handle is retired, because it may already be freed. Destroy the runtime to drain any worker that it still owns. If the cleanup never entered C, the outer handle that the caller owns may stay allocated, because runtime destruction only invalidates it.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The native destroy fails.

finish() → None#

Wait for the asynchronous pipeline to finish, then release the native handle.

A call after finish() or cancel() does nothing.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The native finish or the handle release fails.

is_running() → bool#

Return True while the asynchronous pipeline is still running.

A finished or cancelled pipeline reports False instead of raising. Both terminators drain the run and release the native cookie, because ovclash_suite_async_destroy deletes the handle. The answer then comes from the state this object tracks, not from a poll of a released handle, which the C ABI can only reject.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The native poll fails.

poll() → tuple[bool, PipelineStepData]#

Return the running state and the current step data in one call.

A finished or cancelled pipeline reports False and a cleared, completed step, so both halves agree with is_running() and step_data().

Returns:

(running, step_data).

Raises:

RuntimeError – A native query fails.

step_data() → PipelineStepData#

Return the progress of the active asynchronous pipeline step.

A finished or cancelled pipeline reports a cleared, completed step instead of raising. That answer comes from the state this object tracks, because the native progress call rejects a handle whose engine run was already consumed.

progress is passed through unclamped. On OpenUSD, a poll that races the counter reset of a phase can report a value outside [0, 1] or a non-finite one; clamp it, and treat a non-finite value as unknown.

Returns:

The step data.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The native progress query fails.

class ovclash.python.suite.AsyncFetchAndSave(
runtime: ClashDetection,
destination: Any,
handle: c_void_p,
adapter: Any = None,
notification_path: str = '',
)#

Bases: object

Async fetch-and-save operation that owns its runtime and destination leases until close.

ClashDetection.run_async_fetch_and_save() creates it. finish() and cancel() join the worker and keep the terminal snapshots readable. close() cancels and drains the worker, and releases the handle and every Python owner. Serialize calls that share one operation. Custom serializer hooks run on its worker thread.

Parameters:

  • runtime – ClashDetection whose results are persisted.

  • destination – Suite serializer or ClashData facade that receives the results.

  • handle – Native fetch handle, filled by the launch. This object owns it.

  • adapter – Adapter of a custom serializer, or None for a built-in serializer.

  • notification_path – Store path for modification callbacks, cached before the launch.

cancel() → None#

Cancel and join the worker; work that already completed successfully stays successful.

A closed operation ignores the call.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The call comes from a serializer callback, or the cancel fails. An exception from a serializer callback is re-raised in its place.

close() → None#

Cancel and drain the worker, then consume the handle, even after a cleanup failure.

A processing failure that finish() or cancel() already reported is not raised again. The first failure during close still propagates. An interruption before the native destruction keeps every owner for a retry. Native consumption clears the handle even if Python interrupts the return; a later close then completes the interrupted retirement of the Python owners without calling the native destruction again. A failed cleanup of an already finalized parent keeps its native handle owned, so a later close or runtime destroy can recover it.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The call comes from a serializer callback, or the cancel or the destruction fails. An unreported exception from a serializer callback is re-raised in its place.

finish() → None#

Join the worker and report its outcome; the terminal snapshots stay readable.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The operation is closed, the call comes from its serializer callback, or the operation was cancelled or failed. An exception from a serializer callback is re-raised in its place.

get_counts() → tuple[int, int, bool]#

Return (written, total, initialized); the counts start at zero.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The operation is closed or the native query fails.

get_last_error() → str#

Return the terminal diagnostic of the operation.

The diagnostic is empty while the worker runs and does not change once it is set.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The operation is closed or the native query fails.

get_step_data() → PipelineStepData#

Return a snapshot of the current initialization, fetch or commit phase.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The operation is closed or the native query fails.

is_running() → bool#

Return whether persistence or worker cleanup is still running.

A closed operation reports False.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The native poll fails.

ovclash.python.suite.run_ovstage_owner_operation(
operation: Callable[[...], Any],
/,
*args: Any,
**kwargs: Any,
) → Any#

Run owner SDK work under the process-wide ovstage lifecycle gate of clash.

Calls operation(*args, **kwargs) synchronously on this thread while holding the gate. Acquire this gate before any owner lock. When other clash contexts share the process, route this work through it: Stage creation and destruction, population, source edits, inspection composition, and renderer attach, step and detach. Calls nest on one thread, up to 64 active operations.

Inside the operation, every Suite call that reaches the native library fails, not only the clash runtime calls. ClashQuery and the other model helpers, data stores, exports, and the timestamp and escape utilities fail too, although they touch no runtime. Only nested run_ovstage_owner_operation() calls and last-error reads are allowed.

Parameters:

  • operation – The callable to run.

  • *args – Positional arguments for operation.

  • **kwargs – Keyword arguments for operation.

Returns:

The return value of operation, after the gate is released.

Raises:

  • TypeError – operation is not callable.

  • RuntimeError – The loaded backend lacks this optional extension, which only the ovstage backend exports. Also raised when the nesting limit is exceeded or the native gate fails.

  • BaseException – Any exception that operation raised, re-raised with its original traceback after the gate is released.

Models#

The object model has two sides:

  • input: a query and its point-cloud settings;

  • results: clash records and per-frame records.

ExportColumnDef is the column definition that the export helpers take.

class ovclash.python.suite.ExportColumnDef(order: int, name: str, alignment: bool = False)#

Bases: object

Column definition for the JSON and HTML table exporters.

alignment: bool = False#

True right-aligns the column in HTML export; JSON export ignores it.

name: str#

Column label.

order: int#

Zero-based index of the cell this column reads within each row. Columns are emitted in list order; order does not reorder them. Must be less than the number of columns.

Persistence#

ClashData is the storage facade. It delegates to a serializer:

  • ClashDataSerializerSqlite stores all records in one SQLite .ovclashdb file. Its open(), save() and save_as() also accept a .clashDetection container, the Kit-era file that wraps a SQLite database behind a 16-byte header. ClashData() without an argument creates this serializer.

  • ClashDataSerializerDirectory stores the same records as separate, readable JSON files in a directory.

  • AbstractClashDataSerializer is the contract that a custom serializer implements. Both built-in serializers derive from it.

Persistence walks through the workflow. SQLite serializer and Directory serializer describe the two stores.

class ovclash.python.suite.ClashData([clash_data_serializer])#

Bases: object

High-level data facade for queries, overlaps, frames and point-cloud settings.

With either built-in serializer, a live fetch iterator rejects writes, commits and store lifecycle changes until it is exhausted or closed. Python reads return materialized values and release their native read cursors before they return. Cursors created directly through the C ABI still reject lifecycle changes until they are destroyed. A rejected cleanup keeps the serializer reference; close the dependents and retry. Custom serializers enforce their own lifetime rules. Serialize all calls that share the store; the guards do not make concurrent calls safe. Async fetching reserves reads as well and runs the storage work on its native worker.

The query, overlap, frame and point-cloud methods return the serializer’s result. Without an open store they return 0, an empty container or None.

Mutating methods take commit (default True). commit=False leaves the write pending in the handle’s transaction until commit(), save(), close() or a later write with commit=True commits it. With either built-in serializer, a later write that fails after its storage write began rolls back the whole pending transaction. That includes earlier commit=False writes that returned successfully. A value that the store checks while writing can cause such a failure: a NaN REAL value with the SQLite serializer (the directory serializer stores NaN), a non-finite frame matrix or, with the directory serializer, a string that contains NUL. Other argument, open-state and not-found failures leave pending writes untouched. Validate inputs before a batch, or commit before a write that may fail.

Parameters:

clash_data_serializer – Serializer implementation. When omitted, a closed SQLite serializer handle is created through the Suite C ABI; call open() before file-backed operations. None creates a facade without a store.

CLASH_DATA_FILE_EXT = '.clashdata'#

Extension that the Kit extension gives the temporary database it extracts from such a container. This package extracts to a temporary .ovclashdb instead.

CLASH_DATA_LAYER_CUSTOM_CLASH_DB_PATH = 'clashDbPath'#

customData key on the USD layer of a .clashDetection container that holds the path of the associated database. This package writes no USD, but readers of those layers need it.

CLASH_DATA_LAYER_CUSTOM_MODIFIED = 'clashDbModified'#

customData key on the same layer that records whether the database has unsaved changes.

CLASH_DATA_LAYER_FILE_EXT = '.clashDetection'#

Extension of the legacy container that open(), save() and save_as() of the SQLite serializer accept besides .ovclashdb.

close() → None#

Close the current store; built-in stores first attempt to commit pending writes.

Close fetch iterators first. Closing is not a request to discard pending work. When the commit of a built-in store fails, the store requests a rollback and raises, and it stays available for inspection or retry.

Raises:

RuntimeError – A built-in store fails to commit or close.

commit() → None#

Commit pending changes of the current data store; without an open store, do nothing.

property data_structures_compatible: bool#

Whether the schema of the current store is compatible; True without a serializer.

property data_structures_migration_to_latest_version_possible: bool#

Whether the current store can migrate to the latest schema; True without a serializer.

property deferred_file_creation_until_first_write_op: bool#

Whether file creation waits for the first write; False without a serializer.

destroy() → None#

Close the store and release this facade’s reference to it.

Built-in stores attempt to commit pending writes first. The native handle of the default serializer is destroyed too. A caller-supplied serializer is only closed; its caller still owns it. Close fetch iterators first. A rejected or failed cleanup propagates its error and keeps the serializer reference for inspection or retry.

Raises:

RuntimeError – A built-in store rejects the cleanup or fails to commit or close.

last_error() → str#

Return why the last failure reported without raising happened.

SQLite open() leaves an incompatible database closed, and migrate_data_structures_to_latest_version() returns False; neither raises. This method tells the caller why, so a silently closed store can be told apart from an empty one.

open(file_path_name: str) → None#

Open the store at file_path_name, closing another open store first.

Without a serializer, or with an empty path, the call does nothing. A relative path resolves against the current working directory at each call. The call also does nothing when the serializer’s absolute serializer_path already names the resolved path; the built-in serializers provide serializer_path. Otherwise the open store is closed and the new one is opened. A store opened through a relative path may name a different store after a directory change, so it is always reopened, as is a store whose serializer has no serializer_path.

Parameters:

file_path_name – Path of the store to open.

class ovclash.python.suite.ClashDataSerializerSqlite#

SQLite Suite serializer that stores all records in one .ovclashdb file.

It shares its native fetch and cursor lifetime rules with the directory serializer. It reads and writes legacy .clashDetection containers through the native import and export.

CLASH_DB_FILE_EXT = '.ovclashdb'#

Legacy alias of SERIALIZED_FILE_EXT.

FETCH_ABORT_OVERLAP = 6#

fetch_transaction() operation that returns to the restore point of an overlap.

FETCH_BEGIN = 1#

fetch_transaction() operation that begins pending writes.

FETCH_BEGIN_OVERLAP = 4#

fetch_transaction() operation that saves a restore point before an overlap is streamed.

FETCH_COMMIT = 2#

fetch_transaction() operation that publishes the pending writes.

FETCH_END_OVERLAP = 5#

fetch_transaction() operation that releases the restore point of an overlap.

FETCH_ROLLBACK = 3#

fetch_transaction() operation that discards the whole pending transaction.

SERIALIZED_FILE_EXT = '.ovclashdb'#

Extension of the store file that this serializer writes.

SUPPORTED_CLASH_FRAME_INFO_VERSION = 7#

ClashFrameInfo model version that this serializer stores.

SUPPORTED_CLASH_INFO_VERSION = 18#

ClashInfo model version that this serializer stores.

SUPPORTED_CLASH_QUERY_VERSION = 5#

ClashQuery model version that this serializer stores.

SUPPORTED_POINT_CLOUD_SETTINGS_VERSION = 2#

PointCloudSettings model version that this serializer stores.

Release the native handle after attempting to commit pending writes.

A successful commit publishes the partial results kept after a failed or abandoned fetch. Close fetch iterators first. An explicit native failure keeps the handle for retry. A success, or an uncertain ctypes return, retires the handle before the result is checked.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The commit or the close fails. A failed commit requests a rollback.

fetch_find_overlap(
query_id: int,
overlap_id: str,
) → ClashInfo | None#

Return one stored overlap header by query and hash.

The header needs no frames. While neither this hook nor fetch_write_overlap() is overridden, the adapter snapshots the query’s headers once per fetch operation and serves keys not yet written from that snapshot. A lookup of a key written during the fetch reloads its header by stable identifier, so normalization by the CRUD methods stays visible; if the identity changed, the adapter refreshes the snapshot. Overriding this hook or the write hook keeps lookups live. An indexed override helps stores with many existing rows.

Native fetching preserves review metadata. With state updates enabled, recurring clashes become Active, except Approved clashes whose detected header and complete ordered frame contents are identical; those stay Approved.

Parameters:

  • query_id – Query identifier.

  • overlap_id – Overlap hash.

Returns:

The header, or None when the query has no overlap with that hash. Its identifier must be an integer in the signed 64-bit range other than -1.

Exhaust or close the iterator before the store is closed or reopened, and serialize calls on the same handle. Each frame owns its payload, so it stays valid after the cursor advances or closes.

Parameters:

  • first_frame_offset – Zero-based index of the first frame; a negative offset counts as zero.

Returns:

An iterator over the frames, in order.

fetch_transaction(operation: int) → None#

Execute one FETCH_* transaction operation, or raise.

Custom fetching requires an override; the default raises NotImplementedError.

  • FETCH_BEGIN begins pending writes and is idempotent.

  • FETCH_COMMIT publishes the pending writes.

  • FETCH_ROLLBACK discards the whole pending transaction, including earlier batches and unrelated uncommitted changes. The fetch requests it after a serializer or saved-result reader callback fails while the fetch advances.

  • FETCH_BEGIN_OVERLAP saves a restore point before an incomplete overlap is streamed.

  • FETCH_END_OVERLAP releases that restore point.

  • FETCH_ABORT_OVERLAP returns to the restore point and keeps earlier completed pending writes.

An initialization failure leaves pre-existing writes pending. An extraction or preparation failure requests FETCH_ABORT_OVERLAP only for an incomplete streamed overlap, and a failed abort falls back to FETCH_ROLLBACK; otherwise earlier completed writes stay pending. Closing an unfinished iterator follows the same abort and fallback rules and reports a cleanup failure.

The fetch calls FETCH_BEGIN before the final FETCH_COMMIT, even for an empty result, so a successful fetch publishes pre-existing writes too. It requests a full rollback at most once, so the rollback need not be idempotent. A failed rollback cannot guarantee recovery, and a failure after the side effects of a custom commit may leave durable changes even when the callback raises.

Fetch-and-save is therefore not all-or-nothing in every case. A serializer must implement these semantics; the base class cannot emulate a rollback with CRUD calls.

Parameters:

operation – One of the FETCH_* constants of this class.

Raises:

NotImplementedError – The serializer does not override this method.

fetch_visit_existing(
query_id: int,
) → Iterable[int]#

Return the stored overlap identifiers of a query without loading frames.

The native fetch calls this once when it begins. The default delegates to find_all_overlaps_by_query_id(); a store with an identifier cursor should override it. A store that allows several rows with the same overlap hash must override it, because the hash-keyed CRUD mapping exposes only one identifier per hash.

Parameters:

query_id – Query identifier.

Returns:

The identifiers, each an integer in the signed 64-bit range other than the unsaved sentinel -1.

insert_overlap(
clash_info: ClashInfo | None,
insert_also_frame_info: bool = True,
update_identifier: bool = True,
commit: bool = True,
) → int#

Insert an overlap.

The frames are checked before anything is written, so a frame that the C ABI cannot represent raises ValueError and leaves the store and clash_info unchanged. With frames, the header is written uncommitted and the frame replace applies commit to both. A frame write that the store rejects, such as a non-finite matrix or a storage error, therefore rolls the header back with it. A frame count above the materialization limit of the store is rejected before that write begins and leaves the header pending. clash_info receives its identifier only after success.

Parameters:

  • clash_info – Overlap to insert; None inserts nothing.

  • insert_also_frame_info – Also insert the frames in clash_info.clash_frame_info_items.

  • update_identifier – Write the stored identifier back to clash_info.

  • commit – Commit the write. False leaves it pending.

Returns:

The stored identifier, or 0 for None or a destroyed store.

Raises:

  • ValueError – The C ABI cannot represent a frame.

  • RuntimeError – The store rejects the header or the frames.

is_open() → bool#

Return True when a store is open.

last_error() → str#

Return why the last failure reported without raising happened.

Two methods of this class report failure by returning instead of raising. open() leaves an incompatible SQLite store closed, for reference parity, and callers inspect is_open(). migrate_data_structures_to_latest_version() returns False. Both record the reason that the C ABI produced, so a caller can tell an old-schema store from an empty one, and both clear it when they succeed.

The result is the reason recorded by those calls, not the raw last-error text of the handle. The native error is sticky: it survives a later successful call, so reading it directly can report a stale failure as a current one.

Returns:

The reason, or an empty string when the last such call succeeded.

migrate_data_structures_to_latest_version(
file_path_name: str,
) → bool#

Migrate an existing store to the latest supported schema.

file_path_name names the store to migrate in place; it is not an output path. Migration never creates a missing file, so a path that does not exist yet fails. To put a migrated store somewhere new, migrate the current one and then call save_as().

A directory store validates and reopens the current format; no older directory format can be migrated. An invalid destination manifest leaves the current directory open with its pending writes. A SQLite path that is missing, is not a readable regular file, or names a SQLite file that this process cannot write leaves the open state and the pending writes of the current store unchanged. So does an empty path on a store without a current path, such as an unnamed store.

Migration only reads a .clashDetection container. Passing its path extracts it again to a new temporary copy and deletes any earlier copy of the store. Writes to that earlier copy are lost unless they were exported to the container first. An empty path uses the cached path, which names the container after open() until a save() or save_as() succeeds. To keep those writes, migrate the path of the copy, from get_file_path(), instead.

Parameters:

file_path_name – Store to migrate, or an empty string for the cached path.

Returns:

True after a successful migration. False otherwise, never an exception; then last_error() says why.

property on_modified_fnc: Callable[[str], None] | None#

Callback that runs after modifying operations, or None.

open(file_path_name: str) → None#

Open a store path through the Suite C ABI.

A SQLite store opens a legacy .clashDetection container through the native layer, which extracts it to a temporary .ovclashdb file and opens that file. save() and save_as() can target either a plain .ovclashdb file or a legacy .clashDetection container. A directory store treats every path as a directory, whatever its suffix. An empty path opens an unnamed store; is_open() reports its native state even though get_file_path() is empty. Unnamed stores support CRUD and async fetching.

For legacy SQLite compatibility, an incompatible database does not raise. The store stays closed and last_error() records the reason; callers inspect is_open(), data_structures_compatible() and data_structures_migration_to_latest_version_possible().

Parameters:

file_path_name – Path of the store, or an empty string for an unnamed store.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The open fails for another reason. A live fetch also rejects the open and keeps the current handle and cached path; exhaust or close the iterator before retrying.
