save(
file_path_name: str | None = None,
) → bool#

Save the current store, optionally to a new destination.

Without a destination, save() passes the cached path and the store commits its pending writes. After open() or migrate_data_structures_to_latest_version() of a .clashDetection container, the cached path names the container, so the next save() exports to it again. That stops once a save() or save_as() succeeds, because each success caches the native path, such as the path of the temporary copy. Pass the container path to save_as() to export again.

With a different destination, a SQLite store is backed up there, including committed WAL rows and pending writes. A deferred store whose file does not exist yet adopts the new path instead. A .clashDetection destination receives an exported snapshot, and the current store keeps its path, even the empty path of an unnamed store. After a success, the cached path is read back from the native state.

Parameters:

file_path_name – Destination path. None uses the cached path.

Returns:

True; failures raise RuntimeError.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The save fails. A live fetch also rejects the save, and the previous cached path is kept.

save_as(file_path_name: str) → bool#

Save the current store to a new path.

A directory store adopts the target after a successful save. A SQLite store has the native layer back up its database, named or unnamed, and adopts an ordinary destination after success. An existing alias of the current file keeps its identity; a private legacy extraction may move to the new destination after its connection closes. A .clashDetection target receives a fresh, closed SQLite snapshot, and the source connection and path stay unchanged. After a success, the cached path is read back from the native handle, even the empty path of an unnamed store.

Parameters:

file_path_name – Destination path.

Returns:

True; failures raise RuntimeError.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The save fails. A live fetch also rejects the save without changing the current handle or cached path; exhaust or close dependent iterators first.

class ovclash.python.suite.ClashDataSerializerDirectory#

Directory Suite serializer that stores readable JSON records instead of a SQLite database.

Pass a directory path to open(); a suffix is part of the directory name. Queries, point-cloud settings, clashes and individual frames go to separate JSON files. commit=False keeps edits pending until commit, save or close. Deferred creation leaves a missing directory absent until the first write.

open("") opens an unnamed store. Its private temporary directory is created at the first write when creation is deferred, the default, and at open otherwise. Closing the unnamed store removes that directory; save_as(path) keeps its records in a named directory and makes that directory current.

Pass an instance to ClashData(serializer), or directly to the runtime fetch-and-save. Both built-in serializers follow the same native fetch and cursor lifetime rules. Serialize access to one store, and close live fetch iterators before a commit or a lifecycle change.

FETCH_ABORT_OVERLAP = 6#

fetch_transaction() operation that returns to the restore point of an overlap.

FETCH_BEGIN = 1#

fetch_transaction() operation that begins pending writes.

FETCH_BEGIN_OVERLAP = 4#

fetch_transaction() operation that saves a restore point before an overlap is streamed.

FETCH_COMMIT = 2#

fetch_transaction() operation that publishes the pending writes.

FETCH_END_OVERLAP = 5#

fetch_transaction() operation that releases the restore point of an overlap.

FETCH_ROLLBACK = 3#

fetch_transaction() operation that discards the whole pending transaction.

SERIALIZED_FILE_EXT = ''#

Empty, because a directory store has no file extension.

SUPPORTED_CLASH_FRAME_INFO_VERSION = 7#

ClashFrameInfo model version that this serializer stores.

SUPPORTED_CLASH_INFO_VERSION = 18#

ClashInfo model version that this serializer stores.

SUPPORTED_CLASH_QUERY_VERSION = 5#

ClashQuery model version that this serializer stores.

SUPPORTED_POINT_CLOUD_SETTINGS_VERSION = 2#

PointCloudSettings model version that this serializer stores.

Close the store after attempting to commit pending writes.

The pending writes include partial results kept from failed or abandoned fetches. Close fetch iterators first.

fetch_find_overlap(
query_id: int,
overlap_id: str,
) → ClashInfo | None#

Return one stored overlap header by query and hash.

The header needs no frames. While neither this hook nor fetch_write_overlap() is overridden, the adapter snapshots the query’s headers once per fetch operation and serves keys not yet written from that snapshot. A lookup of a key written during the fetch reloads its header by stable identifier, so normalization by the CRUD methods stays visible; if the identity changed, the adapter refreshes the snapshot. Overriding this hook or the write hook keeps lookups live. An indexed override helps stores with many existing rows.

Native fetching preserves review metadata. With state updates enabled, recurring clashes become Active, except Approved clashes whose detected header and complete ordered frame contents are identical; those stay Approved.

Parameters:

  • query_id – Query identifier.

  • overlap_id – Overlap hash.

Returns:

The header, or None when the query has no overlap with that hash. Its identifier must be an integer in the signed 64-bit range other than -1.

fetch_transaction(operation: int) → None#

Execute one FETCH_* transaction operation, or raise.

Custom fetching requires an override; the default raises NotImplementedError.

  • FETCH_BEGIN begins pending writes and is idempotent.

  • FETCH_COMMIT publishes the pending writes.

  • FETCH_ROLLBACK discards the whole pending transaction, including earlier batches and unrelated uncommitted changes. The fetch requests it after a serializer or saved-result reader callback fails while the fetch advances.

  • FETCH_BEGIN_OVERLAP saves a restore point before an incomplete overlap is streamed.

  • FETCH_END_OVERLAP releases that restore point.

  • FETCH_ABORT_OVERLAP returns to the restore point and keeps earlier completed pending writes.

An initialization failure leaves pre-existing writes pending. An extraction or preparation failure requests FETCH_ABORT_OVERLAP only for an incomplete streamed overlap, and a failed abort falls back to FETCH_ROLLBACK; otherwise earlier completed writes stay pending. Closing an unfinished iterator follows the same abort and fallback rules and reports a cleanup failure.

The fetch calls FETCH_BEGIN before the final FETCH_COMMIT, even for an empty result, so a successful fetch publishes pre-existing writes too. It requests a full rollback at most once, so the rollback need not be idempotent. A failed rollback cannot guarantee recovery, and a failure after the side effects of a custom commit may leave durable changes even when the callback raises.

Fetch-and-save is therefore not all-or-nothing in every case. A serializer must implement these semantics; the base class cannot emulate a rollback with CRUD calls.

Parameters:

operation – One of the FETCH_* constants of this class.

Raises:

NotImplementedError – The serializer does not override this method.

The native fetch calls this once when it begins. The default delegates to find_all_overlaps_by_query_id(); a store with an identifier cursor should override it. A store that allows several rows with the same overlap hash must override it, because the hash-keyed CRUD mapping exposes only one identifier per hash.

The identifiers, each an integer in the signed 64-bit range other than the unsaved sentinel -1.

  • commit – Commit the write. False leaves it pending.

insert_overlap(
clash_info: ClashInfo | None,
insert_also_frame_info: bool = True,
update_identifier: bool = True,
commit: bool = True,
) → int#

Insert an overlap.

The frames are checked before anything is written, so a frame that the C ABI cannot represent raises ValueError and leaves the store and clash_info unchanged. With frames, the header is written uncommitted and the frame replace applies commit to both. A frame write that the store rejects, such as a non-finite matrix or a storage error, therefore rolls the header back with it. A frame count above the materialization limit of the store is rejected before that write begins and leaves the header pending. clash_info receives its identifier only after success.

Parameters:

  • clash_info – Overlap to insert; None inserts nothing.

  • insert_also_frame_info – Also insert the frames in clash_info.clash_frame_info_items.

  • update_identifier – Write the stored identifier back to clash_info.

  • commit – Commit the write. False leaves it pending.

Returns:

The stored identifier, or 0 for None or a destroyed store.

Raises:

  • ValueError – The C ABI cannot represent a frame.

  • RuntimeError – The store rejects the header or the frames.

is_open() → bool#

Return True when the store is open, including an unnamed temporary store.

last_error() → str#

Return why the last failure reported without raising happened.

Two methods of this class report failure by returning instead of raising. open() leaves an incompatible SQLite store closed, for reference parity, and callers inspect is_open(). migrate_data_structures_to_latest_version() returns False. Both record the reason that the C ABI produced, so a caller can tell an old-schema store from an empty one, and both clear it when they succeed.

The result is the reason recorded by those calls, not the raw last-error text of the handle. The native error is sticky: it survives a later successful call, so reading it directly can report a stale failure as a current one.

Returns:

The reason, or an empty string when the last such call succeeded.

migrate_data_structures_to_latest_version(
file_path_name: str,
) → bool#

Migrate an existing store to the latest supported schema.

file_path_name names the store to migrate in place; it is not an output path. Migration never creates a missing file, so a path that does not exist yet fails. To put a migrated store somewhere new, migrate the current one and then call save_as().

A directory store validates and reopens the current format; no older directory format can be migrated. An invalid destination manifest leaves the current directory open with its pending writes. A SQLite path that is missing, is not a readable regular file, or names a SQLite file that this process cannot write leaves the open state and the pending writes of the current store unchanged. So does an empty path on a store without a current path, such as an unnamed store.

Migration only reads a .clashDetection container. Passing its path extracts it again to a new temporary copy and deletes any earlier copy of the store. Writes to that earlier copy are lost unless they were exported to the container first. An empty path uses the cached path, which names the container after open() until a save() or save_as() succeeds. To keep those writes, migrate the path of the copy, from get_file_path(), instead.

Parameters:

file_path_name – Store to migrate, or an empty string for the cached path.

Returns:

True after a successful migration. False otherwise, never an exception; then last_error() says why.

property on_modified_fnc: Callable[[str], None] | None#

Callback that runs after modifying operations, or None.

open(file_path_name: str) → None#

Open a store path through the Suite C ABI.

A SQLite store opens a legacy .clashDetection container through the native layer, which extracts it to a temporary .ovclashdb file and opens that file. save() and save_as() can target either a plain .ovclashdb file or a legacy .clashDetection container. A directory store treats every path as a directory, whatever its suffix. An empty path opens an unnamed store; is_open() reports its native state even though get_file_path() is empty. Unnamed stores support CRUD and async fetching.

For legacy SQLite compatibility, an incompatible database does not raise. The store stays closed and last_error() records the reason; callers inspect is_open(), data_structures_compatible() and data_structures_migration_to_latest_version_possible().

Parameters:

file_path_name – Path of the store, or an empty string for an unnamed store.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The open fails for another reason. A live fetch also rejects the open and keeps the current handle and cached path; exhaust or close the iterator before retrying.

Save the current store to a new path.

A directory store adopts the target after a successful save. A SQLite store has the native layer back up its database, named or unnamed, and adopts an ordinary destination after success. An existing alias of the current file keeps its identity; a private legacy extraction may move to the new destination after its connection closes. A .clashDetection target receives a fresh, closed SQLite snapshot, and the source connection and path stay unchanged. After a success, the cached path is read back from the native handle, even the empty path of an unnamed store.

class ovclash.python.suite.AbstractClashDataSerializer#

Bases: ABC

Persistence contract that ClashData uses for a custom serializer.

An implementation stores queries, overlaps, frames and point-cloud settings, and keeps the shape of the legacy Suite Python API.

Native fetching calls the fetch_* hooks below. By default they run synchronously on the caller’s thread; async fetching runs them on its background worker instead. Progress, modification and timing notifications stay on the thread that advances the generator. The native runtime owns report extraction, ordering and result reconciliation.

Fetching into a custom serializer requires an override of fetch_transaction() with real transaction and savepoint semantics; without one, fetching raises NotImplementedError. Override the other hooks when their default adapters over the CRUD methods are inefficient for your store.

Persisted identifiers that the hooks return must fit a signed 64-bit integer and must not be -1, which ClashInfo reserves for a new unsaved record. The default fetch adapters require the CRUD methods to raise on persistence errors. If a store reports failures through ambiguous return values, override the matching fetch hook and raise there instead, because zero can be a valid identifier or a count of deleted frames.

FETCH_ABORT_OVERLAP = 6#

fetch_transaction() operation that returns to the restore point of an overlap.

FETCH_BEGIN = 1#

fetch_transaction() operation that begins pending writes.

FETCH_BEGIN_OVERLAP = 4#

fetch_transaction() operation that saves a restore point before an overlap is streamed.

FETCH_COMMIT = 2#

fetch_transaction() operation that publishes the pending writes.

FETCH_END_OVERLAP = 5#

fetch_transaction() operation that releases the restore point of an overlap.

FETCH_ROLLBACK = 3#

fetch_transaction() operation that discards the whole pending transaction.

abstract close() → None#

Close the current serializer store.

abstract commit() → None#

Commit pending serializer changes.

abstract data_structures_compatible() → bool#

Return True when the open store matches the supported schema versions.

abstract data_structures_migration_to_latest_version_possible() → bool#

Return True when the open store can be migrated to the latest schema.

abstract deferred_file_creation_until_first_write_op() → bool#

Return True when file creation is deferred until the first write operation.

abstract fetch_all_point_cloud_settings() → dict[int, PointCloudSettings]#

Return all stored point-cloud settings keyed by identifier.

abstract fetch_all_queries() → dict[int, ClashQuery]#

Return all stored queries keyed by identifier.

identifier: int,
frame: ClashFrameInfo,

The frame arrays are copied from the borrowed native report before this hook runs, so the serializer may keep the frame. Calls arrive in source order.

  • frame – Frame to append.

identifier: int,
) → None#

Remove the frames of one overlap without committing; raise on failure.

Parameters:

identifier – Stored identifier of the overlap.

fetch_find_overlap(
query_id: int,
overlap_id: str,
) → ClashInfo | None#

Return one stored overlap header by query and hash.

The header needs no frames. While neither this hook nor fetch_write_overlap() is overridden, the adapter snapshots the query’s headers once per fetch operation and serves keys not yet written from that snapshot. A lookup of a key written during the fetch reloads its header by stable identifier, so normalization by the CRUD methods stays visible; if the identity changed, the adapter refreshes the snapshot. Overriding this hook or the write hook keeps lookups live. An indexed override helps stores with many existing rows.

Native fetching preserves review metadata. With state updates enabled, recurring clashes become Active, except Approved clashes whose detected header and complete ordered frame contents are identical; those stay Approved.

Parameters:

  • query_id – Query identifier.

  • overlap_id – Overlap hash.

Returns:

The header, or None when the query has no overlap with that hash. Its identifier must be an integer in the signed 64-bit range other than -1.

fetch_iter_saved_frames(
identifier: int,
first_frame_offset: int = 0,
) → Iterator[ClashFrameInfo]#

Read the saved frames of one overlap in order for the exact Approved comparison.

The frames are owned and start at the zero-based first_frame_offset; a negative offset counts as zero. The adapter holds one frame at a time. Before a write or a transaction, and when the fetch is abandoned, it closes the iterator if the iterator has close(). After an intervening write it may reopen the iterator at a nonzero offset. Stores whose ranged reads scan the skipped rows should override this with a forward cursor; this compatibility default requests one frame per ranged CRUD call.

Parameters:

  • identifier – Stored identifier of the overlap.

  • first_frame_offset – Zero-based index of the first frame.

Yields:

The saved frames, in order.

Raises:

RuntimeError – A ranged read of the default implementation returns several frames.

fetch_mark_absent(
identifier: int,
resolve: bool,
) → None#

Mark a vanished overlap absent, and optionally RESOLVED, without changing its frames.

Parameters:

  • identifier – Stored identifier of the overlap.

  • resolve – Also set the state to RESOLVED.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The default implementation cannot find or update the stored overlap.

fetch_transaction(operation: int) → None#

Execute one FETCH_* transaction operation, or raise.

Custom fetching requires an override; the default raises NotImplementedError.

  • FETCH_BEGIN begins pending writes and is idempotent.

  • FETCH_COMMIT publishes the pending writes.

  • FETCH_ROLLBACK discards the whole pending transaction, including earlier batches and unrelated uncommitted changes. The fetch requests it after a serializer or saved-result reader callback fails while the fetch advances.

  • FETCH_BEGIN_OVERLAP saves a restore point before an incomplete overlap is streamed.

  • FETCH_END_OVERLAP releases that restore point.

  • FETCH_ABORT_OVERLAP returns to the restore point and keeps earlier completed pending writes.

An initialization failure leaves pre-existing writes pending. An extraction or preparation failure requests FETCH_ABORT_OVERLAP only for an incomplete streamed overlap, and a failed abort falls back to FETCH_ROLLBACK; otherwise earlier completed writes stay pending. Closing an unfinished iterator follows the same abort and fallback rules and reports a cleanup failure.

The fetch calls FETCH_BEGIN before the final FETCH_COMMIT, even for an empty result, so a successful fetch publishes pre-existing writes too. It requests a full rollback at most once, so the rollback need not be idempotent. A failed rollback cannot guarantee recovery, and a failure after the side effects of a custom commit may leave durable changes even when the callback raises.

Fetch-and-save is therefore not all-or-nothing in every case. A serializer must implement these semantics; the base class cannot emulate a rollback with CRUD calls.

Parameters:

operation – One of the FETCH_* constants of this class.

Raises:

NotImplementedError – The serializer does not override this method.

fetch_visit_existing(
query_id: int,
) → Iterable[int]#

Return the stored overlap identifiers of a query without loading frames.

The native fetch calls this once when it begins. The default delegates to find_all_overlaps_by_query_id(); a store with an identifier cursor should override it. A store that allows several rows with the same overlap hash must override it, because the hash-keyed CRUD mapping exposes only one identifier per hash.

Parameters:

query_id – Query identifier.

Returns:

The identifiers, each an integer in the signed 64-bit range other than the unsaved sentinel -1.

A list of the ClashData methods that serializer_data_op marks, as function objects. The decorator appends each method when the ClashData class body runs. The list is public because omni.physxclashdetectioncore.clash_data re-exports it.

Export helpers#

Export shows how columns and rows map to the JSON and HTML output.

ovclash.python.suite.export_to_json(
column_defs: Iterable[ExportColumnDef],
rows: Iterable[Iterable[Any]],
additional_info: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
) → bytes#

Serialize rows to JSON with the Suite C exporter.

Parameters:

  • column_defs – Columns, emitted in this order. The order of each column selects the zero-based cell it reads within every row; it does not reorder the columns.

  • rows – Rows of cell values, each holding exactly one value per column. Cells are converted with str(), and None becomes an empty string.

  • additional_info – Optional metadata name/value pairs included in the export, converted with str() like the cells.

Returns:

The UTF-8 encoded JSON document.

Raises:

  • ValueError – A row does not hold one value per column, or a column order is outside the uint32 range.

  • RuntimeError – The native exporter rejects the input, for example a column order that is not less than the number of columns.

ovclash.python.suite.export_to_html(
title: str,
subtitle: str,
column_defs: Iterable[ExportColumnDef],
rows: Iterable[Iterable[Any]],
additional_info: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
) → bytes#

Serialize rows to an HTML document with the Suite C exporter.

Parameters:

  • title – HTML document title.

  • subtitle – HTML document subtitle.

  • column_defs – Columns, emitted in this order. The order of each column selects the zero-based cell it reads within every row, and alignment right-aligns it.

  • rows – Rows of cell values, each holding exactly one value per column. Cells are converted with str(), and None becomes an empty string.

  • additional_info – Optional metadata name/value pairs included in the export, converted with str() like the cells.

Returns:

The UTF-8 encoded HTML document.

Raises:

  • ValueError – A row does not hold one value per column, or a column order is outside the uint32 range.

  • RuntimeError – The native exporter rejects the input, for example a column order that is not less than the number of columns.

ovclash.python.suite.html_escape(text: str) → str#

Escape text with the HTML escaping rules of the Suite export layer.

Replaces &, <, >, " and ' with &amp;, &lt;, &gt;, &quot; and &#39;, and leaves other characters unchanged.

Parameters:

text – The text to escape. A non-string value is converted with str(), and None becomes an empty string.

Returns:

The escaped text.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The native call fails.

ovclash.python.suite.format_int128_hex(hi: int, lo: int) → str#

Format unsigned high and low 64-bit words as a Suite clash-id hexadecimal string.

The result is 0x followed by lowercase hexadecimal digits without leading zeros, so zero formats as 0x0.

Parameters:

  • hi – The high 64-bit word.

  • lo – The low 64-bit word.

Returns:

The hexadecimal string.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The native call fails.

ovclash.python.suite.make_int128(hi: int, lo: int) → int#

Combine unsigned high and low 64-bit words into one 128-bit integer.

The words are not range-checked. lo must be in [0, 2**64) for the result to equal hi * 2**64 + lo.

Parameters:

  • hi – The high 64-bit word.

  • lo – The low 64-bit word.

Returns:

The combined integer.

System helpers#

These functions wrap Suite C ABI entry points: backend information, the current user name, file operations and the .clashDetection container probe.

ovclash.python.suite.backend_info() → ovclash.python.suite.types.BackendInfo#

Return the backend name and compile-time capability flags of the loaded native library.

Returns:

The backend information.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The native query fails.

ovclash.python.suite.current_user_name() → str#

Return the user name that Suite metadata such as last_modified_by records.

The name comes from LOGNAME, USER, LNAME or USERNAME, in that order, and then from the OS account: the password database entry of the real user ID on POSIX, GetUserNameW on Windows. A value that is not valid UTF-8 is skipped.

Returns:

The user name, or an empty string when no source qualifies.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The native query fails.

ovclash.python.suite.file_exists(path: str) → bool#

Return whether path names a regular file, following symbolic links.

This matches os.path.isfile: an empty or missing path, a directory, another file type or a path that contains a NUL character reports False.

Parameters:

path – Filesystem path to test.

Returns:

True for a regular file.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The native query fails.

ovclash.python.suite.copy_file(
source_path: str,
target_path: str,
follow_symlinks: bool = True,
) → bool#

Copy a file with shutil.copy semantics using the suite C ABI.

A directory target receives the copy under the source’s file name, and an existing target file is overwritten. The source’s permission bits are then applied to the target. With follow_symlinks=False a symbolic-link source is recreated as a link, which fails when the target already exists.

Parameters:

  • source_path – Source filesystem path.

  • target_path – Destination filesystem path.

  • follow_symlinks – When True, copy the linked target for symbolic links.

Returns:

True when the copy and the permission copy both succeeded. False for an empty path, a missing or directory source, a failed copy, or a failed permission copy, which leaves the target already written.

Raises:

RuntimeError – A path contains a NUL character; nothing is copied.

ovclash.python.suite.delete_file(path: str) → bool#

Delete a non-directory entry with os.remove semantics using the suite C ABI.

Symbolic links are not followed: a link is removed, never its target.

Parameters:

path – Filesystem path to delete.

Returns:

True when an entry was removed. False for an empty or missing path, a directory, or a failed removal.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The path contains a NUL character; nothing is deleted.

ovclash.python.suite.probe_legacy_clash_detection_file(path: str) → tuple[bool, bool]#

Probe whether a file is a legacy .clashDetection container.

Parameters:

path – Filesystem path to inspect.

Returns:

A pair (is_legacy_container, has_sqlite_payload). The payload flag only means that the embedded payload starts with SQLite’s file header; it does not validate schema compatibility. A missing path reports (False, False).

Raises:

RuntimeError – The path contains a NUL character.

Settings#

Settings lists every setting of both packages with its default, unit and effect.

ovclash.python.suite.default_run_settings() → RunSettings#

Return the default run settings of the loaded native library.

They equal a default-constructed RunSettings except time_codes_per_second, which is 0.0 here, the single-sample fallback.

Returns:

A new settings object that holds the native defaults.

Raises:

RuntimeError – The native defaults cannot be read.

ovclash.python.suite.run_settings_to_query_settings_json(
settings: RunSettings,
) → str#

Serialize run settings to the legacy query-settings JSON through the Suite C ABI.

Doubles are written with 17 significant digits (printf "%.17g"), so every value round-trips exactly. This is not the shortest form: a default epsilon of 1e-6 comes back as 9.9999999999999995e-07. A C caller that stores this text as a query’s settings_json stores it verbatim, so its spelling is part of that format. ClashQuery keeps its settings as a dictionary and re-encodes them with json.dumps on every write.

Parameters:

settings – The run settings to serialize.

Returns:

The query-settings JSON text.

Raises:

  • ValueError – A setting is outside its accepted range or not finite, time_codes_per_second is negative, or set_times is set and end_time is less than start_time.

  • RuntimeError – The native serializer fails.

ovclash.python.suite.run_settings_to_query_settings_dict(
settings: RunSettings,
) → dict[str, Any]#

Return the legacy query-settings JSON of settings decoded into a dict.

Parameters:

settings – The run settings to serialize.

Returns:

The decoded output of run_settings_to_query_settings_json().

Raises:

  • ValueError – A setting is invalid, as for run_settings_to_query_settings_json().

  • RuntimeError – The native serializer fails.

ovclash.python.suite.DEFAULT_SETTINGS#

The Suite default settings as a dict keyed by SettingId. The import builds it from the native defaults of the loaded library. default_run_settings() returns the same defaults as a RunSettings.

Enums, settings, results and clash record models of the Suite Python API.

class ovclash.python.suite.types.ArrayView(
values: Any = (),
*,
dtype: str = 'float32',
components: int = 1,
)#

Bases: object

Small array container compatible with list, NumPy, and Warp consumers.

The values are copied into a tuple at construction.

Parameters:

  • values – Flat scalar values to expose. An object with tolist(), such as a NumPy array, is converted first; None is empty.

  • dtype – Element type name, "float32" or "uint32". numpy() treats any name other than "float32" as uint32; warp() looks the name up on the warp module.

  • components – Number of scalar components per logical element.

numpy() → Any#

Return the values as a NumPy array with the shape of shape.

The element type is float32 for the float32 dtype and uint32 for any other.

Raises:

RuntimeError – NumPy is not installed.

property shape: tuple[int, ...]#

Shape of tolist() and numpy(), (n,) or (n // components, components).

tolist() → list[Any]#

Return the stored values as a Python list.

warp() → Any#

Return the values as a flat one-dimensional Warp array; components are not grouped.

The element type is the warp attribute named by the dtype.

Raises:

RuntimeError – Warp is not installed.

class ovclash.python.suite.types.StageTimeline(
start_time_code: float,
end_time_code: float,
time_codes_per_second: float,
frames_per_second: float,
)#

Bases: object

Root-layer timeline metadata of the open stage, as USD resolves it.

A Stage attached with ClashDetection.attach_ovstage() reports the timeline fields of its attachment, as supplied. Time codes are the stage’s own units; RunSettings times are seconds, so seconds = time_code / time_codes_per_second. Unauthored time codes read 0.0 and unauthored framesPerSecond reads 24.0. The effective rate resolves authored timeCodesPerSecond, then authored framesPerSecond, then 24.0 on both backends.

property end_time: float#

end_time_code in seconds (0.0 when the rate is not positive).

start_time_code in seconds (0.0 when the rate is not positive).
